description: EXPLORATORY. The Freedman-He complement-genus lower bound on ac(L_k, L) is stated in Komendarczyk (arXiv:0808.1533v1, sec-001-energy-bound.md:216-217) FOR BORROMEAN LINKS -- a qualifier the corpus drops (qou-a9li, qou-b5yi) and which this tranche's own earlier literature ledger dropped before drawing the OPPOSITE conclusion. It is load-bearing: a surface in the complement bounding L_k forces lk(L_k, L_j) = 0 by complement homology, so off the Brunnian class the infimum is over an EMPTY set and the estimate is ill-posed, not merely weaker. Measured on the derived carrier (the canonical atom-word closure): ZERO of its components have all-vanishing pairwise linking, on every isotope and in BOTH crossing-resolution branches. So the handle applies at no component here -- while the one carrier where it does apply is the Borromean L6a4, the census assignment retired as a fit by the 2026-08-29 owner ruling. Scope (b) on the HANDLE, with the invariant cited; eq. (43) and ac(L_k, L) themselves are untouched. Nothing wired.

the_dropped_qualifier.sentence_as_held: asymptotic crossing numbers ac( Lk, L) for borromean links can be estimated below
the_dropped_qualifier.why_it_is_load_bearing: a compact oriented S in R^3 \ L_j with dS = L_k forces lk(L_k,L_j) = 0, since [L_k] = [dS] = 0 in H_1(R^3 \ L_j) = Z and that class IS the linking number. Where some lk != 0 the minimised-over set is EMPTY.

measured_on_the_derived_carrier.carrier: closure of the canonical atom braid word; a connected sum of (2,k) torus links, verified 32/32 in SnapPy (docs/audits/2026-08-25-atom-word-closures-are-not-hyperbolic.md)
measured_on_the_derived_carrier.reading: not one component anywhere satisfies the handle's hypothesis, and this holds in both branches -- so it is not an artifact of how the superposition letters were resolved

the_inversion.handle_applies_to: Borromean links -- in this arc, L6a4 (the A=3 carrier)
the_inversion.L6a4_provenance: the CENSUS assignment, admitted AME-driven (jsj_verification.py), retired by owner ruling 2026-08-29
the_inversion.consequence: the only carrier on which route 2's computable handle works is the one that was retired as a fit; on the derived carrier it does not apply at all
